content.text: [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/stripe-alternatives-nigerian-creators-what-nobody-tells-you|stripe]]'s availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional payment infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Gumroad payhip

Stripe's decision not to support Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ethiopia, and dozens of other countries is not a technical limitation — it is a business decision driven by correspondent banking requirements, local regulatory compliance costs, and risk modeling. PayPal operates the same way. The practical result is that a creator in Lagos with a real product, a real audience, and a real income goal is blocked at the infrastructure level before any transaction ever occurs. [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/understanding-how-kenyan-creators-get-paid-internationally-plain|COREMERCH guide to understanding]]-selling-music-online-accepting-bitcoin-plain-language-2|Understanding Selling]] this is the first step toward choosing a different architecture. The correct response is not finding a compliant workaround inside the conventional system. It is building on infrastructure that does not require banking partnerships, local regulatory agreements, or platform permission to operate. NOWPayments operates on blockchain rails that bypass every one of these constraints.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Gumroad's payout delays, Payhip's withdrawal restrictions, and Lemon Squeezy's geographic unavailability all stem from the same root cause: these platforms operate within the traditional financial system. They process payments through Stripe or PayPal on the backend, which means they inherit every restriction those processors impose. When Stripe does not support your country, Gumroad cannot pay you out — regardless of what the platform's feature list implies. Paddle operates as a merchant of record, which creates additional compliance requirements that make it functionally unavailable in most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not platform-level problems. They are financial system problems that only infrastructure built outside that system can solve.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

NOWPayments operates as a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 cryptocurrencies including Bitcoin, Ethereum, USDT on multiple chains, Solana, BNB on Binance Smart Chain, and Tron. When a buyer initiates payment, NOWPayments creates a unique payment address for that specific transaction, monitors the blockchain in real time, and fires a webhook when payment confirms on-chain. The 0.5% fee is the only cost — no monthly fee, no setup fee, no revenue share, no payout schedule. Funds go directly to the wallet addresses you configure. COREMERCH never touches your wallet or your funds at any point before, during, or after deployment.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure is not a workaround for payment restrictions, it's a permanent structural alternative.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

The asymmetric risk of platform dependency becomes concrete only when the platform acts. While a PayPal or Stripe account is functioning normally, the risk feels theoretical and distant. When it stops functioning — through suspension, policy change, or geographic restriction enforcement — the creator loses their revenue channel instantly, often with funds already inside the platform that cannot be withdrawn. The conventional appeals process rarely reverses these decisions because the original decision was made algorithmically and the human review process operates on the platform's timeline and criteria, not yours. Sovereign infrastructure eliminates this asymmetry entirely. Your Cloudflare Pages storefront cannot be suspended by a payment processor's compliance decision. Your wallet cannot be frozen by anyone.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

Ultimately, the choice of architecture depends on your specific situation and needs. If you're a creator in a restricted country, sovereign commerce infrastructure may be the only viable option. If you're looking for a more traditional platform experience, Gumroad or Payhip may be a good choice. However, if you want more control, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness, sovereign commerce infrastructure is the way to go.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The most important question a reader would ask is: 'How can I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?' The answer is: with sovereign commerce infrastructure, you can deploy your own digital commerce stack, even in restricted countries, giving you full ownership and control over your sales data and processes.
Creators who use sovereign commerce infrastructure own their sales data and processes, giving them full control and flexibility.

If you're looking for more information on how to sell digital products in restricted countries, check out our products page at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html, where you can learn more about Edge Commerce Stack ($197) and other solutions. Additionally, you can read about how to deploy a full digital commerce stack using sovereign commerce infrastructure to reach your global audience.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a digital commerce stack using sovereign commerce infrastructure, follow these steps: (1) choose a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, (2) select a backend logic solution like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, (3) select an order storage solution like Supabase or Google Sheets, (4) select a file delivery solution like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, (5) integrate a payment solution like NOWPayments, and (6) configure your stack for automation and delivery.
